title: test(types): a padded grouping field name is refused on every face that declares grouping (objectui#7347)
body:
Fixes #7347
Clause-②: no

## What this is

Ruling C on #7347 (batch #110 item 5) put the fix at the producer: `@objectstack/spec`'s `GroupingFieldSchema.field` refuses a grouping field name with leading or trailing whitespace (objectstack-ai/objectstack#17360), and objectui#11086 already moved this repository to the spec version that carries it. What was left for objectui is the regression pin that the refusal reaches objectui's own validation faces before any renderer is handed the name, plus one stale docblock sentence.

- `packages/types/src/__tests__/grouping-field-padded-refused-7347.test.ts` (new): on every face that declares `grouping` (`list-view`, `object-gallery`, and `object-view`'s named list views), for each of four parse doors (the tolerant `AnyComponentSchema`, `safeValidateSchema` which is what `objectui validate` runs, the strict `StrictAnyComponentSchema`, and the exported mirror itself), the unpadded control parses green and each padded spelling fails with exactly one issue: code `custom`, path at that entry's `field`. The spec's message is not pinned; code and path are. A census derives from `AnyComponentSchema` which arms declare `grouping` and requires that set to equal the fixture table, so an arm that starts declaring `grouping` is covered or the census goes red.
- `packages/core/src/utils/grouping-fields.ts`: comment only. The sentence calling `GroupingFieldSchema.field` "a bare `z.ZodString`" was false against the installed spec; it now says the field refuses a padded name, names the pin, and says the harvester's trim stays as defence. The trim itself is untouched, as ruled.
- `.changeset/7347-padded-grouping-refused-pin.md`: empty frontmatter (tests and a comment, nothing released).

No reader-side normalization anywhere: grid, gallery and kanban are untouched (ruling C refused that).

## Measured before building (the dispatch's mechanism assumptions)

1. **The installed spec refuses.** In this worktree `node_modules/@objectstack/spec` is 17.5.0 (the only resolved version). `GroupingFieldSchema.safeParse({ field: '  business_unit  ' })` answers one `custom` issue at `field`; `{ field: 'business_unit' }` parses. `GroupingConfigSchema` answers the same issue at `fields.0.field`. Confirmed.
2. **objectui's faces inherit it by construction.** Confirmed for every face that declares `grouping`, and measured rather than read. A walk over the 145 flattened arms of `AnyComponentSchema` (and over every zod export of the published `@object-ui/types/zod` barrel) finds exactly three that declare `grouping` in their own document: `list-view` at `grouping`, `object-gallery` at `grouping`, `object-view` at `listViews.*.grouping`. On each, all four doors refuse the padded name as above and parse the control. The mechanism, checked on the gallery arm: `stripImportedDefaults` does rebuild the enclosing `GroupingConfig` and `GroupingField` objects (their `order` / `collapsed` defaults are stripped, so they are no longer reference-equal to the spec's), but the `field` string node crosses the boundary by reference and carries its one check. No face needed a fix, so no objectui schema source changes here.
   `objectui validate` end to end (the command's `validate()` run from source with `tsx` on JSON files; the CLI `dist` was not built): unpadded `list-view` answers `Schema is valid!` and exit 0; padded `list-view` answers exit 1 with `Code: custom` and `Path: grouping → fields → 0 → field`; padded `object-view` answers exit 1 at `listViews → all → grouping → fields → 0 → field`.
3. **The docblock sentence was false.** Corrected as above; that sentence and nothing else in the paragraph.
4. **`groupByField` is not this card.** Not touched; one reading in the Acceptance notes.

## Tests and gates, at `4d99273`

Run from the worktree root, exit codes captured by redirect before any pipe; heavy runs through the shared verify lock.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/` exit 0: `Test Files  286 passed (286)`, `Tests  6673 passed (6673)`. The pin is in that population (`vitest list packages/types/ --filesOnly` names it).
- The pin alone: `Test Files  1 passed (1)`, `Tests  62 passed (62)` (1 producer case, 3 arms × 4 doors × 5 cases, 1 census).
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/grouping-fields.test.ts` exit 0: `Tests  14 passed (14)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.examples.json && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`; `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the pin once). `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check` exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/core^...' build` exit 0 (that closure is `@object-ui/types`: `dist completeness: 1 package(s) complete`). `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/types^...' build` answers `ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_NO_SCRIPT` (exit 1): that closure holds no package with a build script, so there was nothing to build; not a red gate.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exit 0: `2 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`, empty frontmatter.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:shell-escape-residue`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `type-check:coverage`: exit 0 each. `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`.
- ESLint, narrowed to the two touched source files and shown to exclude nothing: `eslint --print-config` returns a config for both (both inside the linted population); `--format json` reports 2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings; the effective config sets neither `parserOptions.project` nor `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- `@object-ui/cli` suite not run: no `validate` case was added.

## Ablation (one-off, not kept in the tree)

The fix was committed first; each leg went through `ablation-replace.mjs` (the anchor must hit, blob hashes before and after) inside a script carrying an `EXIT INT TERM` restore trap. The pin imports the mirrors by relative path, so the mutated source is what runs (no `dist` in the path).

- **A: the import boundary drops the refinement.** In `imported-defaults.ts`'s leaf arm, every imported `string` leaf was rebuilt as a fresh `z.string()`, which has no checks. Landed: anchor 1 → 0, marker 0 → 1, blob `0fa9694db112` → `ac546120b72e`. Expected: every padded case red and every control green. Observed: `Tests  48 failed | 14 passed (62)`. The 48 are the four padded case names × 12 arm-door pairs; the 14 are the producer case, the 12 controls and the census. Restored: blob back to HEAD's `0fa9694db112`, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **B: an arm starts declaring `grouping`.** `grouping` was added to the `object-grid` mirror. The first attempt was refused by the tool as a no-op (the replacement contained the anchor, so the count stayed at 1; nothing ran) and was re-anchored. Observed: `Tests  1 failed | 61 passed (62)`, the census, whose found set gained `object-grid`. Restored: blob back to HEAD's `091582208cc9`, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Boundary: where this pin does not reach, and why it stays out

On the tolerant face, and so through `objectui validate`, an `object-grid` or `object-kanban` node carrying `grouping: { fields: [{ field: '  business_unit  ' }] }` parses green, and so does `grouping: 42`. Neither mirror declares `grouping`, and `BaseSchema`'s passthrough keeps an undeclared key without judging it. The strict face refuses `grouping` on both by name (`unrecognized_keys`) whatever its value. So nothing is stripping the refinement there; the key is undeclared. `object-grid`'s `grouping` already sits in the parity ledger's `UnmirroredDeclared` entry for `ObjectGridSchema` (the objectui#6152 worklist). `object-kanban` reads `grouping` through its index signature, which `ObjectKanban.tsx`'s own docblock names. Declaring either would change a published face's accept set, which `Clause-②: no` rules out for this card, so both go to the seat in the report and are not changed here. If either is declared later, the census picks it up (leg B shows that).

## Acceptance notes

- In passing (dispatch assumption 4): under the installed spec, a `list-view` with `kanban.groupByField: '  stage  '` is refused `custom` at `kanban.groupByField` on both faces (the unpadded control parses), and `gantt.groupByField` is refused the same way at `gantt.groupByField`. That axis is not this card; nothing here touches it.
- `ListView.tsx`'s grouping-projection comment still calls `GroupingFieldSchema.field` "a bare string". Its point (nothing checks that the name is a declared field) still holds. Not edited here because it is outside this card's file surface; no carrier.
- In-flight overlap: this diff does not touch `objectql.zod.ts`, so it does not intersect PR objectui#10278 or PR objectui#11125.
